description: A pre-arranged Modal for confirming or cancelling a single action — title, body slot, and a Cancel/Confirm footer, with the Confirm button's tone following the action (primary, or danger for a destructive one). Composes the registry `modal` and `button` components directly rather than introducing new dialog anatomy.

props.name: children
props.description: The modal's sub-components (Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, ...).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the modal is open on first render. The component owns the flag
from then on. Omit for closed-on-mount.
Forbidden in controlled mode — use `open` instead.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description:
Called with the new open state whenever it changes (open or close).
Optional in uncontrolled mode — useful purely to observe transitions.
Called with the requested open state whenever the modal wants to open or
close (trigger click, Close button, Esc, click-outside, imperative API).
Required in controlled mode.

props.name: open
props.description:
Forbidden in uncontrolled mode — use `defaultOpen` instead.
The current open state. Must be kept in sync by the parent via `onOpenChange`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref receiving the imperative {@link ModalImperativeApiopen/close handle}.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Render into the consumer's own element (e.g. a router `<Link>`) instead
of the default `<button>`, merging the trigger's ARIA wiring, composed
event handlers, and ref onto it via the Slot pattern.

props.name: children
props.description:
The dialog's body — the confirmation message, or any richer content.
Rendered inside {@link ModalBody`ModalBody`}'s own slot.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Called when the Confirm button is activated. Does **not** close the
dialog itself — drive `open`/`onOpenChange` (or the imperative
`close()` API) from this callback if confirming should dismiss it.

props.name: title
props.type: string & ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | string & Iterable<ReactNode> | string & ReactPortal | string & Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | undefined
props.description: The dialog's title, shown in the header next to the optional close button.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description:
Cancel button label. The Cancel button always closes the dialog (it is
wrapped in `ModalClose asChild`) — there is no separate `onCancel` prop.

props.name: onEscapeKeyDown
props.description:
Fires on the dialog's native `cancel` event when the user presses
Escape. Call `event.preventDefault()` to veto closing and keep the
modal open (e.g. to confirm unsaved changes first).

props.name: onPointerDownOutside
props.description:
Fires on a `pointerdown` whose coordinates land outside the dialog's
bounding rect — i.e. on the browser-painted `::backdrop`. Call
`event.preventDefault()` to veto closing and keep the modal open.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

props.name: showClose
props.description:
Shows a close (×) button in the header, in addition to the Cancel/
Confirm footer actions. Off by default — the exploration found the
footer's Cancel action already covers the "back out" affordance for a
short confirmation, and a redundant close reads as noise.

props.name: size
props.description:
Dialog width, forwarded to `ModalContent`'s own `size`; `data-density`
scales the padding within each size. Defaults smaller than a plain
Modal — a confirmation is a short, low-content surface.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Selects the Confirm button's variant — `default` → `primary`, `danger` →
`danger` — so the action's own tone drives the dialog, not a separate
colour scheme for the dialog itself.

api.description:
`<primitiv-modal>` — the state owner of a modal dialog, built on the native `<dialog>` and its `showModal()`: the browser makes the page behind it inert, paints the `::backdrop` and owns the top layer, and the element adds the rest of the WAI-ARIA Modal Dialog pattern — Tab wraps inside the dialog, Escape and a press on the backdrop close it, and closing hands focus back to the button that opened it.

The root finds its own parts, and only inside itself: a trigger or close part must be a descendant of the `<primitiv-modal>` it works, though it may sit anywhere in it, outside the dialog included, and may arrive later (rows swapped into a list). To open a modal from a button elsewhere on the page, set its `open`. A modal nested in another, inside its dialog or beside it, keeps its own parts; its events still bubble through the outer root, so a listener there checks `event.target`. The root reconciles its parts' ARIA from its reflected state whenever a part arrives, leaves, or changes an attribute the root reads (the lifecycle is `PrimitivRootElement`'s), so content swapped into an open dialog is wired as it lands. Leave `open` off the `<dialog>` itself: the root opens it, modally.

Setting `open` from script fires no `primitiv-modal-change`: the event announces changes the user asks for. However it closes, the dialog hands focus back to what had it when it opened.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the dialog is open. Reflected: it changes as the user opens and dismisses the dialog, so a server re-render or a history snapshot sees the live state. Set it (or the `open` property) to open or close the dialog from script.

events.name: primitiv-modal-change
events.description: Bubbles, cancelable, fired before a user-driven change is applied — a trigger or close click, Escape, a press on the backdrop, or the dialog closing natively — with the open state afterwards. Call `preventDefault()` to veto it, e.g. to keep a form with unsaved changes open.

api.description: `<primitiv-modal-trigger>` — an interactive part. It decorates exactly one child the consumer writes, a `<button>`, which opens the dialog and receives `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, so the rendered DOM matches React's (RFC 0033 D24). A modal may have several.

`<primitiv-modal-content>` — decorates exactly one native `<dialog>` the consumer writes, which the root opens with `showModal()`, closes, and gives an id, `data-state`, and `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` pointing at the title and description. The dialog keeps its implicit `dialog` role.

`<primitiv-modal-title>` — decorates exactly one heading the consumer writes (an `<h2>`, usually), whose id becomes the dialog's `aria-labelledby`, so it is the name a screen reader announces as the dialog opens.

`<primitiv-modal-close>` — an interactive part. It decorates exactly one `<button>` the consumer writes, which closes the dialog. A modal may have several: the header's icon button and the footer's Cancel.
